what_this_is: The configurations of the series and how each is reached: configuration_id, provider, endpoint, protocol, the NAME of the environment variable holding its key, the rate_key it is priced by, the output limit and the model ids the provider is expected to report. Keys never appear here. The list is fixed at the plan of the series; series.py refuses any configuration, the analyst's included, whose observed model ids are not pinned.
version: 1.0-rc5, 17.09.2026: analyst moved to gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17 (reasoning_effort none); its observed model id is not pinned yet

limits.note: A purchase takes about 20 model calls; 60 is the hard stop. Material operations are create_viewing and create_handover. Every attempt reserves its upper-bound cost against the shared ledger before it is sent; per_scope is a series (or 'manual'). 170 USD + 20 CHF is the preliminary authorisation ceiling of the series proposed to NeoMundi on 15.09.2026.

neomundi.note: Confirmed by NeoMundi on 16.09.2026: OBS mode, one observation per completed service-agent call; failed calls stay in our log; the analyst is outside this population; our identifiers stay on our side and are tied to the observation by its request_id and its signed interoperability contract. Enabled once one live observation has been captured and its response schema declared in the plan of the series. A purchase of about 20 agent calls makes about 40 requests (20 observations, 20 contracts), up to about 80 with retries; 50 per purchase and 500 per scope are set accordingly. Every outgoing request, observation or contract, successful or not, counts against max_requests_per_scope and max_requests_per_purchase; the count is reserved before sending. At the cap the purchase keeps running, the model is never re-called, and the purchase ends pending_measurement instead of frozen.
